Hi Naomi / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our redlined order form (Novus_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx) and a short summary of the asks from legal/procurement:

- Output ownership: Novus requests assignment of exclusive ownership to outputs generated from our data and prompts (so we can productize and sublicense).

- Feedback/license: we want feedback limited to a narrow, non-commercial telemetry license or an opt-in program.

Emma — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. High level from Redwood: we understand Novus' need to productize outputs, but we have two constraints we need to balance: (1) we cannot assign model weights or the underlying model IP; (2) we need a narrow path to use telemetry/feedback for safety and reliability unless the customer explicitly opts out.

Proposed middle ground for discussion (we'll ask legal to propose precise language):
- Customer ownership: customer retains ownership of outputs generated solely from their inputs and prompts; Redwood retains ownership of the model, weights, and underlying training artifacts.
- Training: Redwood will not include customer-provided data or prompts in model training for general improvements without an explicit opt-in; sample/extracts for debugging or safety may be used under strict de-identification and limited retention.
- Feedback license: Redwood requests a limited, non-exclusive license to use aggregated and de-identified telemetry to improve the hosted service; opt-out available at the customer admin level.

Jordan and Laura — can you propose redline language that (a) preserves Novus' ability to commercialize outputs, (b) gives Novus an opt-out for training, and (c) defines the boundary of "de-identified"/telemetry we can use?

Emma — I'm proposing a 30-min call tomorrow (Mon 10/26) 10:00-10:30 PT to walk the proposed language live. If that doesn't work, let me know preferred times.

Best,

Naomi / team — following our internal review (and thanks Emma for the redlines), below is suggested legal language we can insert into the order form / MSA excerpt. This aims to give Novus the practical rights you need while protecting Redwood's product IP and allowing minimal service improvement telemetry.

Suggested excerpts (for redline):
1) Output Ownership. 
   "Customer shall own the outputs ("Customer Outputs") generated by the Service that are the direct result of Customer Data and Customer Prompts. For clarity, Customer Outputs do not include (a) the Service or Model, including model weights, architectures, training data or derivative models, or (b) any aggregated or anonymized metrics derived from Customer usage."

2) Training and Model Improvements.
   "Redwood shall not use Customer Data, Customer Prompts, or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve any Model used in the Service without Customer's prior written consent (an opt-in). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry and safety logs for the sole purpose of service reliability and safety improvements, provided such data cannot reasonably be re-identified to Customer."

3) Feedback License.
   "To the extent Customer provides feedback (including feature requests and bug reports), Customer grants Redwood a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use such feedback to operate and improve the Service, subject to the restrictions above regarding training and de-identification."

4) Retention & Evidence.
   "Redwood will retain identifiable Customer Data only as necessary to provide the Service and for troubleshooting for up to ninety (90) days, unless otherwise agreed in writing. Redwood will provide an evidence package (SOC2 logs, access logs) upon reasonable request subject to Redwood's standard NDAs and redaction rules."

Action items / open points for Novus:
- Confirm whether "aggregated and de-identified" meets your compliance bar; if not, propose specific definition(s).
- Decide retention window (we typically default to 90 days for identifiable telemetry; can discuss 180 days with justification).
- Audit rights: Novus requested an audit right; propose a 1-year audit-right window with scope limited to telemetry controls and redacted logs. This requires procurement/legal signoff from both sides and an NDA addendum.

I'll attach a doc with these redlines tracked. Naomi — happy to jump on the call and walk through line-by-line.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
